title: Groups
definition: A command that prints the names of all the groups the current user (or a specified user) is a member of.
simpleExplanation: Checking which teams you are on. If you can't access the 'finance' folder, you run this command to see if you are actually in the 'finance' team.
realWorldExample: You try to run a Docker command but get Permission Denied. You type `groups` and notice 'docker' is not in the list. You realize you forgot to add yourself to the Docker group.

basic: If you type `groups` by itself with no arguments, whose groups does it show?
intermediate: After you add yourself to a new group using `usermod`, you type `groups` and the new group isn't there. Why?

answers.question: Whose groups?
answers.answer: It shows the groups for the currently logged-in user.

answers.question: Why isn't the new group there?
answers.answer: Group memberships are evaluated at login. You must fully log out of the terminal and log back in (or run `newgrp <groupname>`) for the new group membership to take effect.
